reading: The National Railway Museum in Port Adelaide preserves and interprets Australian railway history while operating as a hands-on, family-friendly place to visit. Its world runs from steam locomotives and rolling stock to photographs, oral histories, diagrams and research enquiries; it also offers train rides, school resources, functions and publications. The museum is a self-funded, volunteer-run organisation concerned with care of collections, access, education and keeping railway knowledge alive for future generations. Its vocabulary is practical and affectionate: rolling stock, gauges, shunting, fettlers, the Goods Shed, the Fitch and Fluck Pavilion, collection enquiries and Catch Point. What distinguishes it is the meeting of working railway skills and archive discipline with play: a miniature railway, the Tea and Sugar Train, a seaside railway, a simulator, and a restored 1947 cafeteria car used for parties. The collection spans state, Commonwealth and private operators, while the museum’s volunteers, members and supporters keep the whole enterprise moving.

enemies.idea: The Master Indexer photographs a crew, assigns each member a rolling-stock category, and sends freight wagons to retrieve anyone listed as missing. Its six-month index is always behind reality, so old disguises can confuse it.
enemies.why: A cataloguing system becomes a delayed, exploitable pursuit mechanic.

enemies.idea: Gauge Gangers lay competing 1067 mm and 1435 mm tracks beneath moving feet, forcing vehicles and crew into different routes until the rails are deliberately crossed.
enemies.why: The archive’s actual diagram gauges create a spatial puzzle.

enemies.idea: An Appointment Keeper locks archive doors around visitors and demands they arrive at their own scheduled time; it advances the clock whenever anyone moves.
enemies.why: Access by appointment becomes a tense timing game.

enemies.idea: The Selective Acceptor tests carried objects against its donation checklist, confiscating anything it deems significant enough to preserve and rejecting useful decoys as duplicates.
enemies.why: The real cost of collection care becomes a thieving antagonist with rules to manipulate.

enemies.idea: A pair of Push and Pull machines attach magnetic couplings to opposite ends of a target; each becomes stronger while the other has tension.
enemies.why: Simple machines make a readable cooperative enemy whose link can be broken.

enemies.idea: A runaway train simulator projects the route it expects onto the floor; its railcar drones can only travel on those projected lines, but keep redrawing them ahead of the crew.
enemies.why: A training tool creates a moving battlefield with visible constraints.

enemies.idea: Fettler Box mites scatter quiz answers across the floor, then hammer temporary track through every answer chosen; a correct railway answer lays a safe diversion.
enemies.why: A quiz and track maintenance combine into a fight that rewards observation.

enemies.idea: A Semaphore Dune Runner hauls sand over the seaside line and tunnels through its own drifts, surfacing beside the jetty whenever a whistle sounds.
enemies.why: The railway’s jetty, esplanade and dunes create a distinctive ambush.

enemies.idea: The 1947 Cafeteria Car has become a rolling party trap: its restored doors seal and serving tables slide together to pen guests until the couplings are released.
enemies.why: A specific preserved carriage makes a compact, moving escape room.

enemies.idea: A shunting pack modelled on the ten 800 class locomotives works in concert, coupling obstacles into a barricade and separating anyone who wanders from the group.
enemies.why: Shunting becomes coordinated crowd control instead of a generic train charge.

enemies.idea: Broad Gauge Steam sprawls across two tracks and widens its wheelsets to block a passage; narrow openings and switching points foil its slow turns.
enemies.why: Gauge determines the encounter’s geometry and a clear weakness.

enemies.idea: The Pass Maker extrudes narrow-gauge rails through cracks, then squeezes its jointed carriages into the newly made passages to flank intruders.
enemies.why: The narrow-gauge railway through a pass becomes a terrain-changing flanker.

enemies.idea: The Catch Point presses a fresh mechanical photograph of the crew into a plate; drones follow the pose in that plate rather than the crew’s current positions until the next edition.
enemies.why: Railway photography and a periodic magazine produce a decoy tactic.

enemies.idea: The Boiler Examiner has pressure gauges for eyes and issues basic or advanced qualifications by blasting progressively hotter steam at anyone who approaches its firebox.
enemies.why: A skilled volunteer qualification becomes a legible escalating trial.

enemies.idea: A Risk Assessor labels each floor patch with a possible hazard, then manufactures that hazard to prove its plan correct; removing its chalk marks interrupts the sequence.
enemies.why: The school risk plan creates hazards the crew can anticipate and erase.

enemies.idea: The Gold Member collector sorts people into single, family, junior and overseas parties, locking together anyone it decides belongs in the same category.
enemies.why: Membership types turn into a social sorting puzzle.

enemies.idea: The miniature railway’s Scale Thieves swap full-size points with tiny ones; each switch changes which doors and tunnels are big enough for the crew.
enemies.why: A model railway makes size and route selection matter.

enemies.idea: The Oral History Repeater samples a shouted instruction and broadcasts it later from a different siding, luring its allies toward the echo.
enemies.why: Recorded testimony becomes a sound-based trap the crew can misdirect.

enemies.idea: The Backdrop Shifter rolls historic carriages into place around a target, composing a perfect railway scene and trapping the target inside the frame.
enemies.why: The museum’s working film location becomes a spatial ambush.

enemies.idea: Tea and Sugar Provisioners sweep through the grounds on a supply train, scooping up every loose tool as cargo and dropping crates that open into little repair drones.
enemies.why: A named train and its supplies become a moving resource contest.

enemies.idea: The Old Line Tracer follows the remembered route of the Old Ghan, laying a ghost rail under whoever carries its recovered route notes.
enemies.why: Following a historic line becomes a chase that can be redirected.

enemies.idea: A Maintenance Vehicle patches every damaged swarm machine it can reach, but must park and unfold its workshop arms to make a repair.
enemies.why: A collection category becomes a support enemy with an exposed repair window.

allies.idea: Volunteer fettlers keep a hand-operated set of points free from swarm control and can build a safe detour if the crew brings them spare rail.
allies.why: The museum’s volunteer culture gives the crew a practical foothold.

allies.idea: A sheltered visual narrative, maintained by independent guide machines, shows the next room’s sensory conditions and a calm route through it.
allies.why: Accessibility becomes a respectful, useful means of navigation.

allies.idea: An independent archive steward protects original photographs and offers older track diagrams that reveal routes the swarm has forgotten.
allies.why: Research and preservation provide actionable knowledge.

allies.idea: A volunteer boiler attendant keeps a small steam engine ready as a rescue tug, provided the crew helps find clean water and keeps its firing area clear.
allies.why: Specialist railway knowledge provides a mobile ally with needs.

allies.idea: A self-guided school pack teaches the crew to use a lever and pulley to shift a jammed carriage without waking the machines.
allies.why: The educational material empowers an improvised solution.

bosses.idea: The Grand Accession is a many-carriage archive engine that mistakes preservation for ownership: it captures objects, photographs their surroundings and adds each new record as another armoured wagon. Separate the catalogue car from the locomotive to make it lose track of its acquisitions.
bosses.why: Collections, photographs and rolling stock combine into a boss whose power has a practical dependency.

bosses.idea: The Museum That Runs Forever is a vast swarm assembled from steam and modern rolling stock, model railway points and volunteer workshop tools. It tries to keep every exhibit moving on its own timetable; crews can turn its different gauges and conflicting routes against one another.
bosses.why: The full sweep of railway history becomes a multi-stage system to untangle.

bosses.idea: The Journey Planner converts the entire grounds into a compulsory itinerary, switching between a school lesson, a family ride and a function in the cafeteria car. Each phase has a different rule, and freeing a carriage removes that rule from its final circuit.
bosses.why: The museum’s overlapping purposes become a varied fight that changes as the crew intervenes.

events.idea: A tiny train circles the model layout with a real key tied to its roof; a full-size swarm train copies every switch the crew throws on the model.
events.why: A small choice has a visible, larger consequence.

events.idea: A seaside train is stopped by a drift of sand while a dune runner approaches. Dig it out, reroute it along the esplanade, or use its whistle to draw the runner away.
events.why: A rescue offers several immediate approaches grounded in the coastal line.

events.idea: A volunteer has recovered two nearly identical crossing diagrams in different gauges. The crew must choose the one matching the rails before a maintenance drone arrives.
events.why: Close inspection pays off under pressure.

events.idea: The archive appointment bell rings for a visitor who has not arrived, and the doors will open briefly. The crew can slip inside or hold the doorway for an allied researcher.
events.why: A routine access rule produces a small moral and tactical choice.

events.idea: The cafeteria car is rolling slowly toward a locked gate with a package of spare couplings on board. Catch the car or change the points to bring it safely to a halt.
events.why: The party carriage becomes a moving recovery puzzle.

events.idea: A set of school worksheets asks visitors to find a lever, wheel and pulley. Each working example can also disable a different swarm barricade.
events.why: Exploration teaches practical ways through the site.

events.idea: A simulator keeps replaying a safe route through the pavilion, but its controls are missing. The crew can reconstruct the route from the simulator’s last run or repair the controls.
events.why: A learning resource becomes a navigational puzzle.

events.idea: A boiler attendant’s rescue tug has steam but a jammed coupling; the crew can free it while protecting the attendant from incoming maintenance drones.
events.why: A timed repair can earn transport and a useful ally.

events.idea: A donation examiner has rejected a battered hand tool as a duplicate. Its volunteer owner knows the tool fits an old switch mechanism and asks the crew to recover it.
events.why: Selective collecting creates a personal retrieval job without treating the policy itself as foolish.

events.idea: A Catch Point photograph shows a clear siding, but the latest picture contains one extra wagon. Find the wagon and discover the swarm’s concealed repair station inside.
events.why: A photographic clue invites close comparison.

events.idea: A group of volunteers is holding a set of points by hand while two incompatible gauges of swarm traffic approach. Help them improvise a stop before fatigue wins.
events.why: Human effort and track geometry create immediate urgency.

events.idea: A visual narrative has been mixed with a swarm route plan. Match its landmarks to the actual pavilion to recover a quieter way through.
events.why: A thoughtful access resource becomes a wayfinding clue.

events.idea: A shunter repeatedly rearranges three wagons into the same order. Place an empty wagon in the sequence to make it open a path to the Goods Shed.
events.why: Observing a shunting routine unlocks a nonviolent solution.

events.idea: The Tea and Sugar train is dispensing supplies to both sides. A crew member can uncouple the provision wagon and share its contents with stranded volunteers before it completes its circuit.
events.why: A familiar named train becomes a moving opportunity for aid.

events.idea: A railway history guide points along the Old Ghan Line while a swarm tracer follows the same directions. Alter the trail markers to lead it into a harmless loop.
events.why: A route-following subject becomes a deception opportunity.
